stories.headline: Massive unrest and clashes erupt across France over living costs
stories.body:
French authorities said about 550,000 demonstrators joined cost-of-living protests across the country on Saturday [c3]. The nationwide demonstrations brought together trade unions, school students, and the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement [c10].

Clashes between protesters and police led to two deaths during the unrest [c4]. A 22-year-old police officer died in Nantes after being struck by a vehicle [c4]. A protester also died near Paris [c4]. French authorities reported around 2,400 arrests across the country after the violence [c5]. Police in Paris reported a record 855 arrests in the capital alone [c13]. France's interior ministry said almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes were injured during Saturday's unrest [c8]. Seven of those injured officers were hurt seriously [c8]. On Sunday, police fired tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered at Place de la République in Paris [c9].

Violent incidents occurred in several other parts of France during the demonstrations. An apparent arson attack damaged a 19th-century town hall in the city of Limoges on Saturday [c1]. Firefighters fought the town hall blaze through Saturday night and into Sunday morning [c2]. Limoges Mayor Guillaume Guérin said municipal police ran out of ammunition around 3:30 p.m. while trying to hold off rioters [c14]. Guérin called the incident a colossal failure of the state [c14].

French President Emmanuel Macron gave a televised address on Sunday [c6]. Macron blamed radical far-left factions and criminal elements for the destruction during the protests [c7]. Macron said that those who destroyed must pay [c6]. He said that those who looted must pay back [c6]. He added that those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable [c6].

International figures also commented on the situation in France. US President Donald Trump posted on social media and blamed immigration for the unrest [c11]. Trump said that France is burning [c11]. Protests over the cost of living and public services were not limited to France [c12]. Similar demonstrations also took place in Spain, Italy, and Portugal [c12].

stories.headline: Deadly fire at Canadian military base kills four during training
stories.body:
Four Canadian service members died on Saturday during a military training exercise in Alberta [c16]. A fast-moving fire and explosion occurred at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright [c15]. Soldiers were conducting live-fire combat exercises when a grass fire started about 1 kilometer away [c21]. Major-General Wade Rutland said uncommonly strong winds pushed the fire toward the range administrative area [c21].

The four deceased service members were identified as Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding, and Pte Hayden Lykkemark [c17]. Hospitals admitted 39 patients, with at least 19 in critical condition [c16]. Internal military communications said 31 people were very seriously injured, according to the Globe and Mail [c26].

Alberta's health agency sent 30 units to Wainwright, including 22 ground ambulances, six planes, and two helicopters [c22]. Military medical personnel parachuted into Wainwright shortly before midnight to assist [c24]. Ontario mayoral candidate Cathy Keane said on Facebook that her eldest son was among the critically injured personnel [c25].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the incident one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime [c18]. Carney ordered flags on all federal buildings across Canada to be flown at half-mast [c19]. The Department of National Defence said there were no indications that the fire was a terrorist attack [c20]. Canadian Forces Base Wainwright usually has about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers on site daily [c23].

stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in occupied West Bank
stories.body:
Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats and Palestinian civilians near Taybeh on Saturday [c27]. The targeted delegation included Belgian, French, and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor [c27]. Eyewitnesses said an attacker aggressively shouted "France, France" before pushing French Mayor Bernard Baudoux to the ground [c34]. Settlers smashed a reinforced window of an SUV carrying European diplomats as the vehicle drove away [c35].

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military blamed Israeli rioters for the attack [c31]. The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted a statement titled "Serious accusations require serious evidence" casting doubt on the accounts [c33]. On Friday, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was hospitalized after an assault while covering a Palestinian olive harvest [c28]. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee called for Levine's attackers to be jailed before attending a settler conference on Sunday [c30].

US diplomats including Assistant Secretary of State Riley Barnes and US Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch visited Taybeh on Sunday [c29]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned against a brewing crisis in the West Bank [c36]. Human rights group Yesh Din recorded at least 170 settler attacks on Palestinians since September 27 [c32]. The West Bank is home to about 500,000 Israeli settlers and at least 3 million Palestinians [c37].

vocab.meaning: a group of people sent to represent others

stories.headline: Trump pauses tariffs on nations buying Russian crude energy
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump paused sanctions linked to Russia two days before they were scheduled to take effect [c42]. Trump invoked Section 115 of the Graham Act to certify that waiving sanctions was in the US national interest [c40]. The Graham Act duties included tariffs of up to 500% on Russian goods [c41]. They also included tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest importers of Russian crude oil [c41]. According to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, China receives about 50% of Russia's crude exports, while India receives about 37% [c45].

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump's 60-day waiver decision [c38]. Rubio said India has voluntarily diversified its energy portfolio but still depends substantially on Russian energy [c39]. Trump posted on Truth Social that his decision was aimed at avoiding driving Russia away from peace negotiations [c46]. Trump also temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel to allow fuel into global markets and lower prices [c47].

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the order an important and truly historic moment [c44]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told NBC News that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a historic mistake [c43].

taxes placed on goods brought into a country

stories.headline: Protests erupt in India over voter roll revisions and election official
stories.body:
Protesters staged widespread demonstrations in India against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after a voter roll investigation [c60]. Protests began following a September 23 investigation regarding Election Commissioners' objections to roll revisions [c60]. Civil society organisations including Jan Sarokar, MKSS, Voter Adhikar Manch, and NFIW held a Jan Sunwai public hearing in Batla House [c53].

A public audit of 258 households in Delhi's Okhla constituency found over 100 voters wrongly classified [c52]. The audit showed these voters were marked as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate [c52]. In the Okhla constituency, over 67,000 names were placed on the notice list out of 1.85 lakh draft roll voters [c54]. Nearly 1.6 lakh names in Okhla were placed on the ASDD list [c54].

Political groups and police clashed during related demonstrations. Delhi Police registered three FIRs against protesters for violating prohibitory orders, conducting a flag march, and obstructing police officers [c58]. CRPF Director General GP Singh commended a female CRPF officer for demonstrating restraint after being slapped during a Cockroach Janta Party march [c57]. Mumbai Police detained several people at Carter Road in Bandra who gathered for a Tiranga March called by the Cockroach Janta Party [c59].

Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14 [c62]. Das and Ranka were detained after scaling locked gates at Jantar Mantar [c62]. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke accused authorities of using delaying tactics to prolong the detention of Das and Ranka [c61].

In a related digital rule development, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory on October 10 asking Meta to review its content recommendation systems [c55]. Apar Gupta of the Internet Freedom Foundation criticized the MeitY advisory, calling it a continuing censorship directive [c56].

vocab.meaning: an electoral area and its voters

stories.headline: Actor Tiger Shroff unhurt after gunfire incident in Mumbai
stories.body:
Unidentified assailants opened fire near actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai on Sunday evening [c67]. The shooting occurred at around 7:00 PM near Pushpa Park in Juhu outside a football club [c67] [c70]. Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde said five rounds were fired during the incident [c64]. Shinde visited Shroff's residence on Sunday night [c63].

Shroff suffered injuries to his left hand from gunpowder and glass shards during the firing [c65]. His driver Firdaus sustained a hand injury, and auto-rickshaw driver Chauhan was also injured [c68]. Gangster Anil Pandit posted that he and Harman Sandhu carried out the attack to teach Shroff a lesson [c69]. A video featured Anil Pandit claiming the Lawrence Bishnoi gang targeted Shroff for working with actor Salman Khan [c66].

Lawrence Bishnoi has been in prison since 2015 and is currently in a Gujarat jail [c71]. Anmol Bishnoi was arrested in California in November 2024 and deported to India in November 2025 [c72].

stories.headline: Tragic stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal kills at least 17
stories.body:
A deadly stampede occurred at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata on Saturday evening [c73]. Reports gave different casualty figures for the incident. The Hindustan Times reported that at least 19 people were killed and 25 were injured [c73]. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari reported that at least 17 people were killed, including a seven-year-old girl [c82]. The stampede happened at around 7:40 PM during Saptami celebrations amid sudden rainfall [c79].

Police are examining video footage capturing a microphone warning that the Chorbagan pandal was in poor condition and might collapse [c77]. Local residents in Chorebagan started rescue efforts and carried injured victims to cabs to reach Calcutta Medical College and Hospital [c83].

Chief Minister Adhikari announced a Special Investigation Team headed by a sitting or retired High Court judge to probe the stampede [c74]. Police arrested seven people under charges dealing with culpable homicide not amounting to murder [c76]. The West Bengal government announced a ₹25 lakh ex-gratia payment and a Group D job for the next of kin of each deceased victim [c75]. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ₹2 lakh compensation from the PMNRF for families of the deceased and ₹50,000 for each injured person [c80]. Kolkata Police Commissioner Ajay Kumar Nand imposed Section 163 prohibitory orders on roads adjoining the pandal until October 20 [c78]. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were also imposed in parts of Bowbazar until Tuesday [c81].

the killing of one person by another
